items.title: Shares of FanDuel Parent Slide After Earnings Miss and CEO Resignation
items.summary: Flutter  Entertainment announced the resignation of its longtime CEO Peter Jackson when it reported second-quarter earnings on Wednesday.  Despite a nine-year tenure that saw Flutter grow from a $2 billion U.K.-focused business to a $16 billion international betting titan, Jackson isn’t going out on a high note.  Shares of the world’s largest betting firm and FanDuel parent company were down as much as 12% Wednesday afternoon after the firm reported mixed results and reduced its full-year guidance.

items.title: FCX Flashes Buy Signal; This Is Fueling Copper, Rare Earth Stocks
items.summary: Freeport-McMoRan, Teck Resources and the United States Copper Index Fund ETF were among copper plays flashing buy points on Tuesday.  Rare earth stocks also were lighting up, some with double-digit percentage gains.  The bullish moves in industrial metals comes as oil prices retreat on reported progress toward a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a positive for global growth at a time that the AI infrastructure buildout has U.S. nonresidential construction humming.

items.title: Coinbase vs. CME Group: Which Crypto Stock Is the Better Buy Now?
items.summary: CME Group leads Coinbase on valuation, price gains and near-term growth, even as both expand across crypto and global trading markets.

items.title: Exxon And Chevron Gush Profits Amid Iran War, But Only 1 Oil Stock Rises
items.summary: Chevron earnings more than tripled, easily beating views for the Dow Jones energy giant. Exxon Mobil earnings soared but fell short.

items.title: Investor Reaction to Fed Decision Could Depend on Dissents
items.summary: Interest-rate futures show that traders see a roughly 30% chance that the Fed raises rates versus a 70% chance that it stays on hold, according to CME Group data.  Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack and Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan are expected by many to vote in favor of raising rates.  Investors will also pay close attention to Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh’s post-meeting press conference, although the new Fed leader has been at pains to say little about the direction of rates.

items.title: Stocks Fall on Mideast Escalation Ahead of Fed Rate Decision
items.summary: U.S. stocks are skidding as the Mideast war once again raises the risk of hotter-for-longer inflation, just as Fed governors are meeting to decide on interest rates.
